correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=1, idempotents have zero cyclic character and four two-point source/target intertwining cases yield exact local rank polynomials. Their product is 2^a z^m(1+z)^(m-2d_k); the cyclic 2x2 transfer trace and shift-order count yield F_m(z). Divisor bounds prove the explicit commuting-probability and binomial approximation. Exhaustive direct finite checks through m=5 and type-word equivalence checks through m=7 independently corroborate the general proof and cutoff claims.

originality.rationale: Checked published partition-character idempotent classification (Sarkar–Singh), general idempotent full-transformation centralizer criterion (Araújo–Konieczny), and known binary homometry (Jedrzejewski–Johnson). These are credited, and their recorded implications do not supply the explicit cyclic-character rank-refined centralizer, transfer census, probability bounds or new semigroup application of homometric fingerprints. Search results are evidence of limited coverage, not proof of universal novelty.
residual_risks: The 2013 general full-transformation centralizer criterion is a strong structural predecessor; a more specialized published wreath/cyclic-character enumerator could subsume this result despite not being found.
The eight-point homometric pair and its interval/Patterson data are already known and cannot support independent novelty.
Some historic monoid and centralizer sources may not be indexed; literature searches do not establish uniqueness.

value.rationale: The centralizer rank polynomial is a complete natural commuting invariant for every idempotent in an infinite structured transformation family. The global totient transfer gives a nontrivial sharp exponential commuting-probability law and a conditional binomial rank law, while exact cutoff collisions explain when conjugacy information is lost and connect to established homometry. These findings are not merely recomputation of a known small table.
